name: Lithography
summary: A print from a flat stone or plate on which a greasy drawing takes ink and water repels it; the artist draws as on paper.
how: Draw on the stone with a greasy crayon or a tusche wash; the drawing takes ink and the rest stays wet.
Pull the print in a press at a run of 20 to 200 copies for an artist print, or more for a poster.
Use one stone for each colour; 3 to 5 stones give a poster.
Keep the soft crayon grain and the dark, velvet black.

origin.note: Alois Senefelder invents lithography in Bavaria.

adoptions.via: A press in Tabriz prints the first lithographed Qur'an (AH 1248), and Iranian presses then print books from scribe-written stones.
Honoré Daumier draws crayon lithographs for Le Charivari in Paris.
Jules Chéret prints his first colour posters on his own presses in Paris, with one stone for each ink.
Odilon Redon publishes the lithographs of Dans le rêve, black dream visions.
Henri de Toulouse-Lautrec prints the poster Moulin Rouge: La Goulue in colour lithography.
Raja Ravi Varma founds the Ravi Varma Press and prints oleographs of his paintings from limestone and metal plates.
Edvard Munch prints The Scream as a lithograph.
The state printing works in St Petersburg prints Bilibin's fairy-tale books, with the tints drawn on separate stones.
Shanghai advertisers have yuefenpai calendar posters printed by chromolithography from rubbed charcoal and watercolour originals.
San Francisco poster artists have their dance posters printed by offset lithography, the planographic process on a rotary press.
